title: Comparing Conventional Targeting Versus Tractographic Planning with DRTx Tracking in Unilateral High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HiFUS) Thalamotomy for Essential Tremor: A Randomized Controlled Trial with retrospective Analysis of AI-supported Rubral Wing Visualization
summary:
Essential tremor (ET) is the most common movement disorder in adults, affecting 4–5% of people over the age of 65. High-intensity focused ultrasound (HiFUS) thalamotomy is an effective treatment option for drug-resistant ET. Typically, when planning the procedure with HiFUS technology, imaging techniques are used to identify a specific anatomical target in the brain where the treatment will be applied. Known side effects of the procedure (such as movement disorders) could be due to the fact that this point is the exact target of the treatment. It might be more effective to identify the fiber tracts that cross this point and apply the HiFUS treatment there instead. The aim of this study is to compare the efficacy and safety of conventional planning methods with tractographic planning for fiber tract identification in unilateral HiFUS thalamotomy for essential tremor. In addition,
the potential of AI-assisted treatment planning will be analyzed retrospectively. 
This study is a single-center, prospective, randomized, controlled pilot study with a parallel group design and patient/investigator blinding, as well as a retrospective analysis component. It will be conducted in 40 patients with drug-resistant essential tremor who are eligible for unilateral HiFUS treatment (20 per group).

interventions.name: Tractographic HiFUS treatment Planning with DRTx Tracking

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.	Patients with essential tremor refractory to at least two tremor medications - either by efficacy or side effects.
2.	Suitable for unilateral HiFUS based on standard MR safety guidelines.
3.	Eligibility for HiFUS according to guideline-based decision of interdisciplinary Movement Disorder Conference
4.	Age 18-85 years
5.	Adequate skull bone density (SDR ≥0.4)
6.	Informed consent for study participation after education by study physician
Exclusion criteria:
1.	Contraindications for HiFUS treatment
2.	Contraindications for MRI without sedation (metal implants, pacemaker, claustrophobia)
3.	Prior thalamic intervention (surgical or ablative).
4.	Secondary or atypical tremor
5.	Other neurological diseases with tremor (Parkinson's syndrome, dystonia)
6.	Cognitive impairment (MoCA < 24)
7.	Progressive neurodegenerative diseases
8.	Severe psychiatric diseases
9.	Coagulation disorders or non-pausable anticoagulant therapy
10.	Pregnancy or breastfeeding
